messages:
maria: Heads-up — found a telemetry + billing mismatch when delegated service tokens are used across projects. Usage shows under the token creator's project instead of the actual request-origin project. This breaks per-project quotas and cost dashboards.

anand: ugh. do we have an example trace?

maria: pasted a minimal trace from staging: `svc-token X -> routed via project-B proxy -> generate usage attributed to project-A (token owner)`

maria: probably because the runtime uses `auth.project` for quota attribution (from token claims) and we lose the original requester when proxying.

taylor: is this the delegated flow where one service account mints a short-lived token for another project?

maria: yes. two common flows: 1) service A in proj-A mints to call customer-facing proj-B endpoints; 2) platform tooling that proxies user requests with an org-level service token. Both end up with wrong attribution.

kevin: immediate idea: add an `orig_project` claim to delegated tokens and thread that into the request context. Then attribution prefers `orig_project` when present.

anand: +1 for claim. need to be careful with what the console allows — we don't want people forging orig_project. must be signed by minting service and validated by runtime.

sarah: question on telemetry: if we change attribution logic, dashboards/history will show a jump. we need migration/backfill or annotation so SRE/finance can separate old vs new attribution.

lee: can we append an immutable `delegation_chain` header at request time instead of changing claims? header would be injected by proxy and signed by vault. runtime reads header for attribution/telemetry only.

kevin: header is fine but harder to bootstrap for existing clients (many direct calls bypass proxy). Claim approach is closer to existing JWT flow and easier to validate.

maria: proposed plan: 1) add `orig_project` to minted tokens (only when mint request includes ?orig_project param and caller is allowed), 2) runtime checks signature + allowlist, 3) attribution code prefers `orig_project` for quotas/telemetry, 4) console adds a toggle and migration labeling in dashboards for rollout.

taylor: rollout UX: we should gate by org opt-in. Default keep old behavior until org flips the switch, then new tokens include claim and runtime honors it for that org. That avoids a global discontinuity.

anand: implementation notes: DB will need a small schema bump to store orig_project in historical usage rows or a separate attribution table. Also need metrics telemetry flagging `attribution_source=claim|default`.

kevin: can we avoid backfill if we store both attribution_project and canonical_project on new rows? console can show a column for "attributed project (new)" and fall back to canonical for old rows.

maria: yes, store both. backend SDKs for dashboards will use `attributed_project` when present. We'll add a migration doc for finance folks.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for auth-server v1.82 to staging at 2024-07-20T16:22:10Z :rocket:

lee: security check: make sure `orig_project` can't be used to escalate quotas (e.g., minting service in proj-A claiming orig=proj-B to consume proj-B's quotas). We'll only accept orig_project when minting identity has explicit delegation permission in org policy.

anand: agree. add policy test and unit tests: `mint_token(caller, target_proj, orig)` must verify `caller` has `delegate_to(orig)` in ACL.

kevin: telemetry/team question: do we want a separate metric for delegated consumption vs native? would help spot abuse.

sarah: yes, add `delegated=true/false` and `delegation_depth` (0 for native, 1 for one-hop) to metrics. Dashboards can filter.

maria: UX items for console: in the quota page show both "Consumed by (reported)" and "Consumed by (token owner)" for orgs with the opt-in. For billing export CSV add a new column `attributed_project` and `delegation_flag`.

lee: operational concern: caching/batching in runtime — we must ensure cached KV prefixes are keyed by the attributed project where relevant, else results could leak or be misattributed. Patch runtime cache keys to incorporate `attributed_project` when present.

anand: noted. that also impacts performance tests — add e2e perf with delegation on/off.

maria: timeline proposal: week 1: spec + policy checks; week 2: auth-server + mint API change + runtime read support (staging); week 3: metrics + console toggles + canary in prod for a subset of orgs; week 4: org opt-in window + docs + billing export changes.

kevin: sounds reasonable. who owns the console toggle? product or eng-platform?

taylor: product owns UX copy and rollout cadence, eng-platform implements backend and console wiring. I'll own console PR and the rollout playbook.

maria: owners: maria (design + runtime), anand (auth-server + policy), taylor (console + rollout), kevin (billing export + metrics), lee (security review).

opsbot: ci-bot: auth-server tests: 112 passed, 3 flaky. See pipeline: https://ci.internal/redwood/auth-server/4823

kevin: one more ask: update the quota docs to specify precedence rules: 1) attributed_project claim, 2) delegation header if present and validated, 3) token owner project, 4) org default. Clear precedence avoids ambiguity.

maria: agreed. I'll draft the doc and ping finance + SRE for review. Anything else?

anand: add a tiny CLI helper to mint sample tokens with `orig_project` for QA. saves time.

maria: good call — I'll add to devtools. Thanks everyone :thanks: 

lee: ok, moving this to a tracked RFC in the repo. PRs incoming. :shipit:
